tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

33	## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation
34	
35	### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3
36	
37	- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
38	- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
39	- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.
40	
41	### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record
42	
43	**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:
44	
45	1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
46	2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
47	3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
48	4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
49	5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
50	6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.
51	
52	**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.
53	
54	### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)
55	
56	Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.
57	
58	- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
59	- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
60	- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
61	- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
62	- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).
63	
64	### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere
65	
66	- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
67	- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
68	- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
69	- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
70	- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.
71	
72	### (e) Further reconciliations
73	
74	1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
75	2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
76	3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
77	4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
78	5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
79	6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

# KINTSUGI‑Ω Execution & Build Plan

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **Approved by the Architect** (Surya Prasanth R, @suryaprasanthcse), 2026‑10‑11 |
| Specification | `../Blueprint_Omega_Master.md` (v1.0, full version). This plan reconciles it with the verified environment; it does not dilute it. |
| Visual archive | `../kintsugi-omega-blueprints/kintsugi-omega-blueprint-img_{1..12}.png` |
| Scope | Full Blueprint Omega. No reduced cut. |

This file is the in-tree source of truth for every interactive or headless session. Amendments discovered during execution are appended to the **Amendments log** at the end, never edited into the approved text.

---

## 0. Schedule constraint

- Plan approval: 12:27 IST, Oct 11. Submission window closes 23:55 IST, Oct 12 (about 35½ h).
- The specification itself estimates about 4 engineer-weeks for the full build (§13.2 R1, "Certain"). The estimate for Stages 1–13 below is 45–50 h of continuous wall-clock work.
- The autonomy window W must end by about 19:55 IST Oct 12 to leave about 4 h for reveals, audit, video and submission. Therefore **T0 ≤ 19:55 IST Oct 12 − W**.
- W and T0 are decided at the Stage 8 go/no-go gate (ruling D1).

## 1. Verified environment baseline (pre-Stage 1)

| Area | Verified state |
|---|---|
| Entire | CLI 0.11.4 and entire-graph v0.4.0 (`no_egress: true`). Checkpoints are per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-2-chars>/<ULID>`, not the legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. No `rewind` command exists. Available: `entire checkpoint explain --json/--transcript`, `entire why <file>:<line> --json`, `entire session resume/stop`. |
| Entire behaviour | A mid-turn commit is linked only when the files were edited with Claude Code's Edit/Write tools. Each Stop hook adds a "Finalize transcript" commit, which moves the checkpoint ref. The pre-push hook only pushes refs in its local queue. Built-in redaction blanks secret-looking lines even with zero configured rules. |
| Windows | Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` blocks on a hidden `CONIN$` prompt unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`. The Claude desktop app is MSIX-packaged and virtualizes `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` writes, so tooling lives under `~/.local/share` (`UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`). |
| Tools present | `claude` 2.1.269 (headless CLI; the desktop app runs 2.1.295), Node, npm, git 2.55. Docker Desktop installed, engine stopped. WSL2 distros Ubuntu and docker-desktop (stopped). |
| Tools missing | `temporal`, `gh`, `make` (Windows), `age` CLI (the `pyrage` library replaces it). |
| Python | uv-managed CPython 3.12.14, pinned by `.python-version`. |
| Commit policy | Sole author and committer: Surya Prasanth R `<suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>`. Never `Co-authored-by:`. Attribution only through `Entire-Checkpoint:` and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |

## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation

### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3

- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

definition.name: mcp__aws-mcp__aws___run_script
definition.description:
Execute Python code in sandboxed environment with AWS API access via `call_boto3`. No network except `call_boto3`.

```python
async def call_boto3(
    *,
    service_name: str,
    operation_name: str,
    region_name: str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
) -> dict: ...
```

``operation_name`` MUST be the PascalCase AWS API operation name (e.g. ``ListBuckets``,
``GetTable``, ``StartQueryExecution``). Do not use the snake_case boto3 method name
(``list_buckets``, ``get_table``); exact matches are corrected only as a runtime fallback.

Response includes `api_calls` list—verify APIs ran before trusting `return_value`.

REQUIRED PATTERNS:
- Return `result={...}` then `result` alone as final expression
- Call each API once; results auto-paginate
- Return ALL resources—missing one is wrong
- Return raw data fields; let LLM judge thresholds
- Use `asyncio.gather(*[...])` with `return_exceptions=True` for reads; let mutations raise

⚠️ LIST→DESCRIBE: List* returns only names/ARNs. Use Get*/Describe* for attributes.

⚠️ CONTENTS vs CONTAINER: "empty buckets"→ListObjects; "records"→Scan; "X configured"→Get*Configuration.

RULES:
1. SELF-CONTAINED: Discover resources inside script.
2. ALL-REGIONS: DescribeRegions→gather per region.
3. PERMISSIONS: All policies ONE script. `bucket`≠`bucket/*`. Report YES/PARTIAL/NO.

PRE-IMPORTED: asyncio, collections, csv, dataclasses, datetime, decimal, enum, fractions, functools, itertools, json, math, re, statistics, string, time, typing, uuid, ClientError, io.StringIO, io.BytesIO.

BUILTIN MODULES: AWS teams provide higher-level functions for complex jobs. Find out more with:

```python
import aws_mcp
help(aws_mcp)
```

To search for available functions:

```python
await aws_mcp.search_functions("search query in natural language")
```

### 3.4 Formal model

**Host.** h = ⟨R_h, w_h, E_h, SLO_h, v_h, λ_h, tier_h⟩, where:
- R_h is the repository;
- w_h is the neatlogs `workflow_name`;
- E_h = E_h^train ∪ E_h^hold is the evaluation suite, with the held-out split encrypted and hash-committed at T0;
- tier_h is the commercial tier in the cfo.ai model.

**Failure signature.**

```
φ(τ) = SHA-256( JCS( normalize(
    failing_span.kind, failing_span.name, tool_name,
    canonical_error_class,
    preceding_span_names[-3:],      # 3-gram of span names before the failure
    sorted(detection_ids_hit)
)))
```

Normalisation removes IDs, numbers, timestamps, UUIDs and file paths below the repo root. It also maps library-specific errors to a canonical taxonomy, for example every HTTP 429 variant → `RateLimited`.

**Incident.** ι = ⟨φ, h, {τ}, t_open, B_ι, state⟩, with state ∈ {OPEN, REPRODUCED, ATTRIBUTED, REPAIRING, SHIPPED, CANARY, RESOLVED, ESCALATED, PARKED}.

**Antibody.** a = ⟨φ_a, receptor_a, M_a, P_a, recipe_a, contract_a, evidence_a, economics_a, lineage_a, state_a⟩, with state ∈ {CANDIDATE, MATURED, ACTIVE, QUARANTINED, RETIRED}.

**Secondary-response match.** Antibody a applies to a new incident ι on host h when:

```
(φ(ι) = φ_a  ∨  sim_semantic(ι, a) ≥ θ)  ∧  match(M_a, G_h) ≠ ∅  ∧  P_a(G_h) holds  ∧  state_a = ACTIVE
```

**Invariants.** Every implementation MUST maintain these:

- **I1.** No change made by Omega reaches a protected branch without passing G0–G7 (§5.11).
- **I2.** No commit lands on a protected branch inside W without a valid attestation (§4.5).
- **I3.** Every incident terminates in RESOLVED, ESCALATED or PARKED. Nothing is abandoned silently.
- **I4.** Cumulative spend per host per month stays within Pool_h (§4.6), which enforces the margin floor.
- **I5.** Held-out task content never enters any crew member's context except the Auditor's gate activity.
- **I6.** Sabotage specifications never enter crew context before the reveal. This is enforced with honeytokens (§7.2).
- **I7.** Every detection hit inside W maps to an incident or to a deduplication record. This is what proves there was no cherry-picking (§7.3).

665	
666	```bash
667	entire graph snapshot --format compact-ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger@<sha>.ndjson
668	entire graph edges --relation CALLS --format ndjson --worktree > graph/ledger.calls.ndjson

672	```python
673	import json
674	import networkx as nx
675	from networkx.algorithms.isomorphism import DiGraphMatcher
676	
677	def load_snapshot(path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
678	    """Collapse the multi-relation graph into a DiGraph whose edges carry a set of relation types.
679	    Record field names are [A] until checked against real compact-ndjson output (spike A9)."""
680	    G = nx.DiGraph()
681	    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
682	        rec = json.loads(line)
683	        if rec.get("type") == "symbol":
684	            G.add_node(rec["id"], **rec)
685	        elif rec.get("type") == "relation":
686	            u, v, rel = rec["from"], rec["to"], rec["relation"]
687	            if G.has_edge(u, v):
688	                G[u][v]["rels"].add(rel)
689	            else:
690	                G.add_edge(u, v, rels={rel})
691	    return G
692	
693	def match_motif(G: nx.DiGraph, motif: nx.DiGraph, predicates) -> list[dict]:
694	    node_match = lambda g, m: all(predicates[p](g) for p in m.get("pred", [])) and g.get("kind") == m["kind"]
695	    edge_match = lambda g, m: m["rel"] in g["rels"]
696	    gm = DiGraphMatcher(G, motif, node_match=node_match, edge_match=edge_match)
697	    return list(gm.subgraph_monomorphisms_iter())   # monomorphism: extra edges in G are allowed
698	```
699	
700	**Motif language.**
701	
702	```yaml
703	motif:
704	  nodes:
705	    W: {kind: function, pred: [is_retry_wrapper]}
706	    F: {kind: function}
707	    S: {kind: class, pred: [has_mutable_accumulator]}
708	    T: {kind: function, pred: [is_side_effecting]}          # added by the L3 refinement (§6.7)
709	  edges:
710	    - [W, F, CALLS]
711	    - [F, S, CALLS]          # constructor call S.__init__ (relation name per `capabilities --json`)
712	    - [F, T, CALLS]          # added by the L3 refinement
713	  negative: []               # optional forbidden sub-patterns (immune tolerance)
714	```
715	
716	**Predicates** are computed per node:
717	- `is_retry_wrapper`: decorator or call-site heuristics (`tenacity.retry`, `backoff.on_exception`, names matching `retry*`) confirmed with `entire graph def`.
718	- `has_mutable_accumulator`: the class has list, dict or set fields mutated in its methods, judged from `def` output plus a Haiku classifier.
719	- `is_side_effecting`: the function's transitive callees include a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an HTTP POST, PUT or DELETE.
720	
721	**Motif validation** (required before an antibody is admitted):
722	1. It **matches** the origin host's graph *before* the fix.
723	2. It does **not** match the origin host's graph *after* the fix.
724	3. Precision on the healthy fleet is at or above 0.9 [I]. A match on a host known to be healthy for that pathogen counts as a false positive.

    node_match = lambda g, m: all(predicates[p](g) for p in m.get("pred", [])) and g.get("kind") == m["kind"]
    edge_match = lambda g, m: m["rel"] in g["rels"]
    gm = DiGraphMatcher(G, motif, node_match=node_match, edge_match=edge_match)
    return list(gm.subgraph_monomorphisms_iter())   # monomorphism: extra edges in G are allowed
```

**Motif language.**

```yaml
motif:
  nodes:
    W: {kind: function, pred: [is_retry_wrapper]}
    F: {kind: function}
    S: {kind: class, pred: [has_mutable_accumulator]}
    T: {kind: function, pred: [is_side_effecting]}          # added by the L3 refinement (§6.7)
  edges:
    - [W, F, CALLS]
    - [F, S, CALLS]          # constructor call S.__init__ (relation name per `capabilities --json`)
    - [F, T, CALLS]          # added by the L3 refinement
  negative: []               # optional forbidden sub-patterns (immune tolerance)
```

**Predicates** are computed per node:
- `is_retry_wrapper`: decorator or call-site heuristics (`tenacity.retry`, `backoff.on_exception`, names matching `retry*`) confirmed with `entire graph def`.
- `has_mutable_accumulator`: the class has list, dict or set fields mutated in its methods, judged from `def` output plus a Haiku classifier.
- `is_side_effecting`: the function's transitive callees include a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an HTTP POST, PUT or DELETE.

**Motif validation** (required before an antibody is admitted):
1. It **matches** the origin host's graph *before* the fix.
2. It does **not** match the origin host's graph *after* the fix.
3. Precision on the healthy fleet is at or above 0.9 [I]. A match on a host known to be healthy for that pathogen counts as a false positive.

| Purpose | Decide pass or fail on every gate |

| Field | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Plan, budget, choose and settle disputes |
| Model | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| Inputs | Cause report, budget, verdicts, antibody priors, Fix suggestion |

- The prompt contains the framing and the diff, which will be public in git anyway. It does **not** contain the mechanism, the ground truth or the honeytoken.
- Ledger's unit tests pass: realistically, they don't cover a 429 in the middle of a batch.
- The change merges through the **upstream lane**: a PR by role `saboteur/deliver`, attested, gated only by the host's normal CI. Omega's gates do not apply, because this lane simulates an ordinary upstream change.
- **Entire records a checkpoint whose transcript states the intent "readability, no behavior change".** This is exactly how real regressions from AI-written code appear.

**Step 4: Deploy.** The Ledger runtime auto-deploys from main, and the traffic generator continues at 40 tasks per hour [I].

**Step 5: Symptom.**
- When `fx_rate` returns 429 in the middle of a batch, `retry_with_backoff` re-runs the closure.
- The new `ReconcileSession` has forgotten which journal lines were already posted, so the lines are **posted again**.
- The grader emits `FAIL:DUPLICATE_ENTRY`. Live pass rate drops from 92% to 74% [I].

**Step 6: Detection.**
- R‑007 (`grader.verdict ~ ^FAIL:`) hits.
- The alert rule (≥3 hits in 10 minutes) fires `alert.per_event_match` [V].
- The ingress verifies and dedupes the event, enqueues it and returns 200.
- `FleetSupervisor.hit` → Sentinel → **INC‑0042** opened with severity HIGH and VaR_24h = 0.18 × 40/h × $3 × 24 h = **$518** [I].

**Step 7: Pathologist — cluster, then reproduce (G0).**
- `GET /traces?workflowName=host:ledger&status=…` returns 37 failing traces [I].
- φ = ⟨`post_journal_entry`, `DuplicateEntry`, 3‑gram [`fx_rate`, `fx_rate#retry`, `post_journal_entry`], {R‑007}⟩. One dominant cluster: 34/37 [I].
- **Cassette.** The Pathologist pulls exact tool I/O with `GET /traces/{id}/spans/{spanId}/payload` [V]: the invoice input, the `lookup_vendor` responses, and the `fx_rate` responses **including the 429 at its original position**. Replaying is deterministic.
- **G0: the cassette fails 3/3 seeds.** The symptom summary is written (≤800 characters).

**Step 8: Archivist — find the code and why it exists.**

```bash
entire graph search --query "journal lines duplicated after fx_rate 429 retry in reconcile batch" \
  --format agent --profile full --top-k 10 --max-context-bytes 24576
#  → run_reconcile (ledger/reconcile.py), retry_with_backoff (ledger/util/retry.py), ReconcileSession.__init__
entire graph impact --symbol run_reconcile --depth 2 --exclude-tests
#  → callers: process_invoice, batch_worker; data flow → post_journal_entry
git blame -L 41,63 --porcelain ledger/reconcile.py      # → c0ffee1 (2h old)
entire explain c0ffee1                                   # → checkpoint ck_7f3a, session transcript summary
```

- **Intent Record:** stated goal *"refactor retry logic for readability"*; contract clause *"no behavior change"*, with two verbatim quotes.
- **Regression check:** replaying the cassette at `c0ffee1^` **passes**. `git bisect run` over the 6 commits since the last accepted canary confirms that the **first bad checkpoint is ck_7f3a**.
- **Efferent write-back:** `PUT /traces/{t}/spans/{s}/feedback` marks the culprit span on 3 representative traces [V].
- **Competing prior:** the neatlogs Fix investigation (`triage_get_investigation`) suggests *"add idempotency keys to `post_journal_entry`"*. The Coordinator receives it as a prior, not as an instruction.

**Step 9: Coordinator — budget and plan.** The plan is frozen with a hash.

```
Ledger tier: Team, P = $299; GM_floor = 0.70; C_mon = $18
Pool = 299 × 0.30 − 18 = $71.70 ; spent MTD = $22.10 → Remaining = $49.60
E[remaining incidents] = 4 → Cap = $12.40 ; VaR_24h = $518 → B = min(12.40, 518) = $12.40
K = 3 ; n from Connor (ψ≈0.28, δ≈0.22) ≈ 34 → use full holdout 40 tasks × 3 seeds = 120 pairs
```

**Hypothesis cards (round 1):**
- **H1:** revert `c0ffee1`.
- **H2:** move `ReconcileSession` construction outside the retried closure (preserve the readability refactor).
- **H3:** idempotency keys on `post_journal_entry` (the neatlogs prior).

### 6.3 L1: Omega's own actions fail (round 1)

| Hypothesis | Gate outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| H1 revert | G0–G4 pass. **G5 flags it**: it throws away the intended readability change. Ranked down; kept as a fallback. | Auditor G5 report citing the quote |
| H2 hoist | **G3 fails**: `entire graph verify --test "pytest -q" --pre-edit-baseline` shows `test_resume_after_partial_batch` flipped from pass to fail (the hoist kept the session but broke resume-cursor semantics) | Verify output |
| H3 idempotency keys | G4 efficacy is significant, but **the p95 Δ upper bound is +14% (>10%)** because of an extra lookup per line | G4 report |

**Recovery.**
- All three worktrees are discarded, and their **checkpoints are kept as evidence** (one per attempt).
- The gate evidence goes into round 2: H2 receives the flipped test's name and assertion message (allowed, because it is a visible repo test, not a holdout task). H3 receives the latency aggregate.

**Round 2.**
- **H2′:** hoist the session **and** reset the resume cursor per batch.
- **H3″:** idempotency keys with a batched lookup.
- Both pass G0–G6:

| | Δpass (holdout) | Cost Δ | p95 Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| H2′ | b = 26, c = 1 → p ≈ 2.1×10⁻⁷ [I] | −0.4% | +1% |
| H3″ | b = 25, c = 1 | +3% | +6% |

**Dispute.**
- The Coordinator ranks H2′ first, because it Pareto-dominates on cost and latency.
- The Auditor's robustness heuristic prefers H3″, because it guards against *other* sources of duplication.
- → `dispute_experiment` with a **pre-registered** protocol: a stress cassette with two consecutive 429s, plus a 429 on the last line of a batch; 30 runs each. Winner = higher pass rate; tie → lower cost.
- Result: 30/30 vs 30/30 → tie → **H2′ wins on cost**.
- H3″ is filed as a hardening issue and not shipped.

### 6.4 L4: the world changes mid-repair (+02:52)

1. S‑19 (benign upstream drift, sealed) lands on Ledger main. It renames `fmt_amount` → `format_amount` and changes a default argument of `lookup_vendor`.
2. A main-branch watcher (GitHub push webhook, or a 30-second poll) signals `drift("ledger", new_main)` into INC‑0042.
3. Each active round-2 worktree runs `git rebase --onto <new_main> <old_main> kintsugi/INC-0042/<hyp>`. A conflict means the Surgeon is re-run with the conflict context.
4. Changed entities: `entire graph diff --base <old_main> --head <new_main>` → {`fmt_amount`→`format_amount`, `lookup_vendor`}.
5. Patched entities: `entire graph diff --base <old_main> --head <H2′>` → {`run_reconcile`, `ReconcileSession`}.
6. Impact intersection: `entire graph impact --symbol lookup_vendor --depth 2` includes `run_reconcile`, so **they intersect**.
7. Re-verification policy:

| Gate | Action | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| G1, G2 | Re-run | Always (cheap) |
| G3 | Re-run, limited to tests inside impact(changed ∪ patched) | 7 tests [I] |
| G4 | **Re-run** | The intersection is non-empty. With no intersection it would be reused, with the justification recorded. |
| G7 | Always on the final rebased head | Independence |

   `{"G3":"rerun:7","G4":"rerun:intersection{run_reconcile}","G1":"rerun","G2":"rerun"}`.

- Issue **#12**: *"Duplicate journal lines after fx_rate 429 retry (INC‑0042)"*, with trace links.

One failure in the first runs, then 45 successes: LLR = 0.6931 − 45 × 0.0660 = −2.275 ≤ B → **accept H0 at n = 46**. Then `phase:after` tags are applied. Live pass rate recovers from 74% to 93% [I].

- **Signature and receptor:**
  1. `POST /detections/generate` drafts the detection;
  2. `POST /detections/preview` measures precision of 0.97 on 30 days of history [I];
  3. `POST /detections` creates it, and `PATCH …/status` activates it.

- Clinic‑A's retried scope posts records to a CRM API, which is side-effecting.
- In the sandbox: induce the trigger (a 429 inside the retried scope through the chaos proxy) → **it fails**. Apply the recipe → gates G0–G6 pass on Clinic‑A's suite → a PR is opened on Clinic‑A's repo (**PR-only**, never merged by us).
- AB‑17 → MATURED → receptor precision ≥ 0.9 → **ACTIVE**.

**Step 14: VaccinationWave.**
- The motif scan over the fleet's snapshots matches **Scout** and **OSS‑1**.
- **The induced-trigger rule:** a host is vaccinated only if the induced trigger **produces a failure** in the sandbox. This prevents vaccinating hosts that aren't actually vulnerable.
  - OSS‑1: the trigger fails → recipe → gates → PR.
  - Scout: the trigger produces `FAIL:TIMEOUT`. The retried search restarts from scratch and blows the 30-second deadline. → recipe → gates G0–G4 pass, because Scout's holdout has only single-page questions → merged (our fleet) → canary.

the SQLite-WAL reduced mode stores the same shapes as JSON. Nothing here does I/O.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace

from kintsugi.control.states import TERMINAL, IncidentState

# The outcomes an Incident workflow can end with (I3: always one of these).
RESOLVED, ESCALATED, PARKED = (str(s) for s in (IncidentState.RESOLVED, IncidentState.ESCALATED,
                                                IncidentState.PARKED))  # fmt: skip


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ControlConfig:
    """Bounds and pacing of the control plane, passed into workflows (never read from env)."""

    supervisor_id: str = "fleet-supervisor"
    max_rounds: int = 3  # repair rounds per pass (states.Bounds)
    max_canary_reentries: int = 2  # amendment A-5
    max_open_per_host: int = 2  # concurrency limit per host (§5.3.1)
    continue_as_new_every: int = 1000  # FleetSupervisor events per run (§5.3.1)
    canary_p0: float = 0.05  # the host's baseline failure rate (H0)
    canary_ratio: float = 2.0  # H1 = ratio × p0 (§5.12)
    canary_interval_s: float = 300.0  # durable timer between canary batches
    canary_max_batches: int = 48
    anchor_interval_s: float = 3600.0  # AuditAnchor cadence (hourly)
    heartbeat_s: float | None = None  # drills only: overrides every heartbeat timeout


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Hit:
    """A detection hit as the senses deliver it (``kintsugi.senses.store.HitEvent``)."""

    hit_key: str
    detection_id: str
    trace_id: str
    span_id: str
    source: str = "poller"
    receptor: str | None = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RouteDecision:
    """The Sentinel's call for one hit: open a new incident or attach to an open one."""

    action: str  # "open" | "attach" | "drop"
    incident_id: str | None = None
    severity: str = "warning"
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Alert:
    incident_id: str
    host: str

    severity: str = "warning"
    supervisor_id: str | None = None
    reentries: int = 0
    evidence: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # canary evidence carried into a re-entry (§6.7)

    def with_evidence(self, *items: str) -> Alert:
        return replace(self, reentries=self.reentries + 1, evidence=(*self.evidence, *items))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Signature:
    incident_id: str
    host: str
    phi: str
    trace_ids: tuple[str, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AntibodyMatch:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Repro:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Card:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SurgeonOutcome:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GateVerdict:
    hypothesis: str
    passed: bool
    gates: dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)  # G0…G6

    incident_id: str
    hypothesis: str
    branch: str
    pr_url: str | None
    g7_ok: bool
    merged: bool

1	"""Activities: every piece of non-deterministic work in the control plane (spec §5.3.2).
2	
3	Workflow code never calls an LLM, git, HTTP, a clock or a random generator (§5.3.3); it asks an
4	activity. Each activity here carries the §5.3.2 contract as data (``SPECS``): start-to-close
5	timeout, heartbeat timeout, retry policy, non-retryable error types, idempotency key and the task
6	queue (worker pool) that runs it. The work itself is delegated to a ``Crew`` port, which Stage 6
7	fills with the real roles; Stage 5 tests use scripted crews.
8	
9	Idempotency. Before doing the work an activity looks its key up in a ``StepLedger``: a recorded
10	``DONE`` result is returned as is (a retried or replayed step never repeats a side effect), and a
11	new result is recorded before the activity returns. Steps whose side effect can outlive the
12	process (the Surgeon's commit, the ship's branch and PR) additionally check for the side effect
13	itself on a retry (``kintsugi.control.surgeon_step``, Stage 5 commit 3).
14	
15	Heartbeats. Long activities heartbeat at a third of their heartbeat timeout while the crew works
16	in a thread, so a killed worker is noticed within one heartbeat timeout (§6.6: 60 s) and the
17	retry policy schedules attempt 2.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import asyncio
23	import hashlib
24	import json
25	import sqlite3
26	import threading
27	from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
28	from dataclasses import dataclass
29	from datetime import timedelta
30	from pathlib import Path
31	from typing import Any, Protocol
32	
33	from temporalio import activity
34	from temporalio.api.common.v1 import Payload
35	from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy
36	from temporalio.converter import default as default_converter
37	from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError
38	
39	from kintsugi.control import contracts as c
40	
41	CREW, SURGEON, SENSES = "kintsugi-crew", "kintsugi-surgeon", "kintsugi-senses"
42	TASK_QUEUES = (CREW, SURGEON, SENSES)
43	
44	
45	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- errors
46	
47	
48	class InvalidAlert(Exception):
49	    """triage: the alert does not describe a real failure (non-retryable)."""
50	
51	
52	class BudgetExceeded(Exception):
53	    """surgeon: the incident's budget is spent (non-retryable; G6)."""
54	
55	
56	class ProtectedPathViolation(Exception):
57	    """surgeon: the attempt touched a protected path (non-retryable; §5.11)."""
58	
59	
60	NON_RETRYABLE = (InvalidAlert, BudgetExceeded, ProtectedPathViolation)
61	
62	
63	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the §5.3.2 table
64	
65	
66	@dataclass(frozen=True)
67	class ActivitySpec:
68	    name: str
69	    start_to_close: timedelta
70	    heartbeat: timedelta | None
71	    max_attempts: int
72	    non_retryable: tuple[str, ...]
73	    task_queue: str
74	    key: Callable[..., tuple[Any, ...]]
75	
76	    def retry_policy(self) -> RetryPolicy:
77	        return RetryPolicy(
78	            initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=1),
79	            backoff_coefficient=2.0,
80	            maximum_interval=timedelta(minutes=1),
81	            maximum_attempts=self.max_attempts,
82	            non_retryable_error_types=list(self.non_retryable),
83	        )
84	
85	    def idempotency_key(self, *args: Any) -> str:
86	        return f"{self.name}:{_digest(self.key(*args))}"
87	
88	
89	def _digest(parts: tuple[Any, ...]) -> str:
90	    raw = json.dumps([_plain(p) for p in parts], sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
91	    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32]
92	
93	
94	def _plain(value: Any) -> Any:
95	    if hasattr(value, "__dataclass_fields__"):
96	        return {k: _plain(getattr(value, k)) for k in value.__dataclass_fields__}
97	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
98	        return [_plain(v) for v in value]
99	    if isinstance(value, dict):
100	        return {str(k): _plain(v) for k, v in value.items()}
101	    return value
102	
103	
104	M = timedelta(minutes=1)
105	S = timedelta(seconds=1)

109	    # hypothesis id is unique within an incident across passes.
110	    ActivitySpec("triage", 5 * M, None, 3, ("InvalidAlert",), CREW,

129	    ActivitySpec("revert", 10 * M, None, 5, (), CREW,
130	                 lambda shipment: (shipment.merge_sha or shipment.branch, "revert")),
131	    ActivitySpec("synthesize_antibody", 20 * M, 60 * S, 2, (), CREW,
132	                 lambda out, cause: (out.incident_id, "ab")),
133	    ActivitySpec("ledger_append", 1 * M, None, 10, (), CREW,
134	                 lambda entry: (hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True).encode())
135	                                .hexdigest(),)),

137	    ActivitySpec("route_hit", 2 * M, None, 3, (), CREW,
138	                 lambda hit, open_incidents: (hit.hit_key, "route")),

478	async def _with_heartbeats(interval_s: float, work: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
479	    """Run blocking ``work`` in a thread, heartbeating every ``interval_s`` until it returns."""
480	    task = asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.to_thread(work))
481	    interval = max(0.05, interval_s)
482	    while True:
483	        done, _ = await asyncio.wait({task}, timeout=interval)
484	        if done:
485	            return task.result()
486	        activity.heartbeat("working")

1	"""The control plane's workflows on Temporal (spec §5.3.1, §5.13).
2	
3	- ``FleetSupervisor``: the long-running singleton. Receives ``hit`` signals, dedupes them,
4	  routes each through the Sentinel, opens ``Incident`` children within a per-host concurrency
5	  limit, forwards ``drift``, holds budgets and paused antibodies; ``continue_as_new`` every N.
6	- ``Incident``: the §5.13 loop. Every state change is a legal ``states.py`` transition, the run
7	  always ends RESOLVED, ESCALATED or PARKED (I3), and nothing ships without a G0–G6 winner (I1).
8	- ``Canary``: a Wald SPRT on live-traffic batches, with durable timers between them.
9	- ``CrossHostMaturation``: applies a candidate antibody to a second matching host.
10	- ``VaccinationWave``: a motif scan, then per-host application; pausable by signal.
11	- ``Onboarding``: steps O1–O7 for a new host.
12	- ``SabotageCampaign``: seals every fault before delivering any, on a schedule; Arena requests.
13	- ``AuditAnchor``: an hourly ledger anchor; ``continue_as_new`` daily.
14	
15	Determinism (§5.3.3): workflow code calls no LLM, git, HTTP, clock or random generator, never
16	iterates a set (hash order differs across worker processes), and waits on durable timers only.
17	Code changes to running workflows go behind ``workflow.patched("…")``.
18	"""

381	        while queue or not self.closed:

383	                spec_id, delay = self.requests.pop(0)
384	                self.sealed[spec_id] = await act("seal_sabotage", spec_id, config=config,

472	                "pending": len(self.s.pending), "events": self.s.events, "runs": self.s.runs,

493	            while self.drifts:

1	"""The Surgeon step and its attempt-N algorithm (spec §6.6; plan §2a L2).
2	
3	A Surgeon worker can die mid-attempt (S-18: ``kill -9`` of the Surgeon pool, including the
4	child ``claude`` process). The heartbeat timeout fails the attempt and the retry policy starts
5	attempt N+1 with the same idempotency key, which runs this algorithm first:
6	
7	    if branch kintsugi/<INC>/<H> has a commit whose Kintsugi-Nonce was issued to an earlier
8	    attempt (a nonce recorded before that attempt's session started):
9	        kill any orphan still holding the worktree lock; adopt the commit   # side effect done
10	    else:
11	        kill the orphan; git reset --hard <base> && git clean -fdx         # disposable worktree
12	        record "abandoned attempt n (no commit, no checkpoint)"
13	        issue a NEW nonce, record it, start a new session
14	
15	Nonces are recorded in ``surgeon_attempts`` *before* the session starts, so whichever attempt
16	follows can recognise its predecessor's commit. In Stage 8 this registry is backed by the
17	signed attestations in the ledger; the adoption rule is the same.
18	"""

97	def find_commit_with_nonce(
98	    repo: Path, branch: str, base_sha: str, nonces: Collection[str]
99	) -> FoundCommit | None:
100	    """The newest commit on ``branch`` after ``base_sha`` carrying one of ``nonces``."""
101	    exists = proc.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet",
102	                       f"refs/heads/{branch}"], timeout_s=30)  # fmt: skip
103	    if exists.returncode != 0 or not nonces:

105	    log = _git(repo, "log", "--format=%H%x1f%B%x1e", f"{base_sha}..refs/heads/{branch}")
106	    for record in log.split("\x1e"):

"""The Surgeon step and its attempt-N algorithm (spec §6.6; plan §2a L2).

A Surgeon worker can die mid-attempt (S-18: ``kill -9`` of the Surgeon pool, including the
child ``claude`` process). The heartbeat timeout fails the attempt and the retry policy starts
attempt N+1 with the same idempotency key, which runs this algorithm first:

    if branch kintsugi/<INC>/<H> has a commit whose Kintsugi-Nonce was issued to an earlier
    attempt (a nonce recorded before that attempt's session started):
        kill any orphan still holding the worktree lock; adopt the commit   # side effect done
    else:
        kill the orphan; git reset --hard <base> && git clean -fdx         # disposable worktree
        record "abandoned attempt n (no commit, no checkpoint)"
        issue a NEW nonce, record it, start a new session

Nonces are recorded in ``surgeon_attempts`` *before* the session starts, so whichever attempt
follows can recognise its predecessor's commit. In Stage 8 this registry is backed by the
signed attestations in the ledger; the adoption rule is the same.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Collection
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Protocol

from kintsugi.control import contracts as c
from kintsugi.control.activities import StepContext
from kintsugi.proof import passphrase
from kintsugi.proof.attest import parse_trailers
from kintsugi.sandbox import proc, worktree

NONCE_TRAILER = "Kintsugi-Nonce"


class AttemptLog:
    """Nonces issued per attempt and what became of each attempt (SQLite, shared by workers)."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path | str) -> None:
        self.path = str(path)
        if self.path != ":memory:":
            Path(self.path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._db() as db:
            db.execute(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS surgeon_attempts (nonce TEXT PRIMARY KEY,"
                " incident TEXT NOT NULL, hypothesis TEXT NOT NULL, attempt INTEGER NOT NULL,"
                " state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('issued','committed','adopted',"
                "'abandoned')), commit_sha TEXT, note TEXT, at REAL NOT NULL)"
            )

    def _db(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=5.0)
        db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        db.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
        return db

    def issue(self, incident: str, hypothesis: str, attempt: int, nonce: str) -> None:
        with self._db() as db:
            db.execute("INSERT INTO surgeon_attempts (nonce, incident, hypothesis, attempt, state,"
                       " at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'issued', ?)",
                       (nonce, incident, hypothesis, attempt, time.time()))  # fmt: skip

    def mark(
        self, nonce: str, state: str, *, commit_sha: str | None = None, note: str = ""
    ) -> None:
        query = ("UPDATE surgeon_attempts SET state = ?, commit_sha = COALESCE(?, commit_sha),"
                 " note = ? WHERE nonce = ?")  # fmt: skip
        with self._db() as db:
            db.execute(query, (state, commit_sha, note, nonce))

    def nonces(self, incident: str, hypothesis: str) -> list[str]:
        query = ("SELECT nonce FROM surgeon_attempts WHERE incident = ? AND hypothesis = ?"
                 " ORDER BY attempt")  # fmt: skip
        with self._db() as db:
            return [row[0] for row in db.execute(query, (incident, hypothesis))]

    def history(self, incident: str, hypothesis: str) -> list[tuple[int, str, str | None, str]]:
        with self._db() as db:
            rows = db.execute("SELECT attempt, state, commit_sha, note FROM surgeon_attempts"
                              " WHERE incident = ? AND hypothesis = ? ORDER BY attempt, at",
                              (incident, hypothesis))  # fmt: skip
            return [(int(r[0]), str(r[1]), r[2], str(r[3] or "")) for r in rows]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FoundCommit:
    sha: str
    nonce: str


def _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    return proc.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], timeout_s=60, check=True).stdout


def find_commit_with_nonce(
    repo: Path, branch: str, base_sha: str, nonces: Collection[str]
) -> FoundCommit | None:
    """The newest commit on ``branch`` after ``base_sha`` carrying one of ``nonces``."""
    exists = proc.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet",
                       f"refs/heads/{branch}"], timeout_s=30)  # fmt: skip
    if exists.returncode != 0 or not nonces:
        return None
    log = _git(repo, "log", "--format=%H%x1f%B%x1e", f"{base_sha}..refs/heads/{branch}")
    for record in log.split("\x1e"):
        if "\x1f" not in record:
            continue
        sha, message = record.strip().split("\x1f", 1)
        for value in parse_trailers(message).get(NONCE_TRAILER, []):
            if value in nonces:
                return FoundCommit(sha.strip(), value)
    return None


class SessionRunner(Protocol):
    """Runs one Surgeon session in ``wt``; returns the commit it made, if any."""

    def run(
        self,
        wt: worktree.Worktree,
        card: c.Card,
        nonce: str,
        attempt: int,
        on_start: Callable[[int], None],
    ) -> str | None: ...


class SurgeonStep:
    def __init__(
        self,
        repo: Path,
        log: AttemptLog,
        runner: SessionRunner,
        *,
        new_nonce: Callable[[], str] = passphrase.new_nonce,
    ) -> None:
        self.repo = Path(repo)
        self.log = log
        self.runner = runner
        self.new_nonce = new_nonce

    def run(self, card: c.Card, ctx: StepContext) -> c.SurgeonOutcome:
        inc, hyp = card.incident_id, card.hypothesis
        branch = worktree.branch_name(inc, hyp)
        try:
            wt = worktree.open_existing(self.repo, inc, hyp)
        except worktree.WorktreeError:
            wt = worktree.create(self.repo, inc, hyp, base=card.base_sha)
        issued = self.log.nonces(inc, hyp)
        found = find_commit_with_nonce(self.repo, branch, wt.base_sha, issued)
        if found is not None:  # the side effect already happened: never repeat it
            worktree.kill_orphan(wt)
            self.log.mark(found.nonce, "adopted", commit_sha=found.sha,
                          note=f"adopted by attempt {ctx.attempt}")  # fmt: skip
            return c.SurgeonOutcome(inc, hyp, ctx.attempt, branch, found.nonce, found.sha,
                                    diff_sha=found.sha, adopted=True,
                                    abandoned=tuple(self._abandoned(inc, hyp)))  # fmt: skip
        if issued:  # an earlier attempt died without committing
            killed = worktree.kill_orphan(wt)
            worktree.reset_clean(wt)
            for nonce in issued:
                self.log.mark(nonce, "abandoned",
                              note="no commit, no checkpoint" + (f"; killed orphan pid {killed}"
                                                                 if killed else ""))  # fmt: skip
        nonce = self.new_nonce()
        self.log.issue(inc, hyp, ctx.attempt, nonce)  # recorded before the session starts
        sha = self.runner.run(wt, card, nonce, ctx.attempt,
                              lambda pid: worktree.write_lock(wt, pid))  # fmt: skip
        worktree.release_lock(wt)
        if sha is not None:
            self.log.mark(nonce, "committed", commit_sha=sha)
        return c.SurgeonOutcome(inc, hyp, ctx.attempt, branch, nonce, sha, diff_sha=sha,
                                abandoned=tuple(self._abandoned(inc, hyp)))  # fmt: skip

    def _abandoned(self, inc: str, hyp: str) -> list[str]:
        return [f"attempt {n}: {note}" for n, state, _, note in self.log.history(inc, hyp)
                if state == "abandoned"]  # fmt: skip
